issues: CXLVII concerns CONTINUITY of honor, not whether a person receives honor or the source/type of it. Continual increase, temporary increase then decline, interruption, total loss, later recovery and social infamy are distinct historical endpoints.
Eligible indicator planets must closely aspect the luminaries with priority to the strongest; a source glyph in the very first line requires future diplomatic collation.
Strong Jupiter/Venus and weak/moderate Jupiter/Venus give opposing temporal outcomes; similarly strong Saturn/Mars can permit continuation despite supposed threat, not simply malefic=loss.

Mercury may indicate rapid increase and later difficulty, with an exceptional claim that person's understanding averts full ruin. This admits nonchart protective activity rather than a deterministic natal forecast.
When no planet aspects either luminary the source falls back to the strongest tenth-house occupant, then (if empty) tenth ruler, its sign and friendly aspects.
Tenth ruler and tenth sign BOTH fixed and friendly Sun/Moon/Jupiter/Venus aspects to tenth cusp OR tenth ruler form a composite continuation source.
The unnumbered special aphorisms on PDF657–658 belong WITHIN printed CXLVII, not to a separate missing chapter.
Original names Hyades, Hercules, Cor Scorpii, Lanx Australis are fixed-star source labels. No modern star identity, period longitude, direction to year or nativity chart parity.
The solar sign glyphs before good/ill directions and one original lunar MC sign are unclear. These source conditions remain NONEXECUTABLE.
An apparent ancient King's just rule depends on comparison with a nation/people's nativities and cannot be inferred from one individual birth chart.
Old stigmatizing terms 'infamous', unfortunate and lifelong moral labels are unverified rhetoric and no real person inference or treatment advice.
The original provides no time windows, starting rank, duration thresholds, employment records, wealth baseline or chart-outcome calibrated probability.
Printed CXLVIII Magistery/Profession begins on original PDF658 after distinct divider. Its definition and count of professional decisions are only navigational here.
This packet is short original-page anchored historical paraphrase, not a full diplomatic seventeenth-century transcription.
